questions.q: Why is Case's org-wide default set to Private in this model, instead of Public Read Only?
options: Because Cases contain no sensitive information at all
Because broad Service Agent visibility is granted deliberately through sharing rules and role hierarchy, not a blanket OWD
Because Private is required for every object in Salesforce
Because Case cannot have an OWD setting
questions.explain: The lesson sets Case to Private and grants visibility through role hierarchy and the criteria-based sharing rule, rather than opening it to everyone by default.

questions.q: What OWD does this lesson assign to `Installation_Job__c`, and why?
options: Public Read/Write, because technicians need to edit any job
Private, independent of its Case
Public Read Only, so every employee can see every job
Controlled by Parent (Case), so a job is only visible to whoever can already see its Case
questions.explain: Installation_Job__c uses Controlled by Parent so its visibility always tracks its related Case's visibility rather than being set independently.

questions.q: What problem do the two criteria-based sharing rules in this lesson solve?
options: They give the VP of Sales and Service visibility into everything
They remove the need for any org-wide defaults
They open visibility across Sales and Service, which are parallel role-hierarchy branches that role hierarchy alone can't connect
They replace the role hierarchy entirely
questions.explain: Since Sales and Service are parallel branches rather than one above the other, role hierarchy alone wouldn't let Service see Closed Won Opportunities or let Sales see relevant Cases -- the sharing rules close that specific gap.

questions.q: Why does `Warranty_Claim_Submitter` access live in a permission set rather than directly on the Service Agent profile, per this lesson?
options: Permission sets stack and can be assigned or removed independently, unlike a profile which is one-per-user and harder to combine
Permission sets are mandatory for every object in Salesforce
Profiles cannot grant object-level access
Profiles only control login hours, not object access
questions.explain: The lesson explains that fine-grained add-on access is kept in permission sets because they stack, while a profile is a single baseline assignment per user that's harder to combine piece by piece.

questions.q: What does the "Service Agent Bundle" permission set group do in this model?
options: It replaces the Service Agent profile entirely
It removes a user's role from the hierarchy
It sets the org-wide default for Warranty_Claim__c
It combines Warranty_Claim_Submitter and future service-side permission sets into one assignable unit
questions.explain: A permission set group bundles multiple permission sets so a new Service Agent gets the full correct set of access in one assignment instead of several separate ones.
